selector.rationale: The presence of a firm, non-tender, mobile mass in the right lower quadrant and a large hypoechoic lesion in the right adnexa, along with a well-marginated thin-walled solid-cystic lesion, supports the diagnosis of massive ovarian edema. Normal tumor markers and the absence of strong evidence for malignancy also favor this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Malignant Ovarian Tumor
rejected.why: Normal tumor markers and lack of strong evidence for malignancy

rejected.label: Ovarian Neoplasm
rejected.why: Less specific than massive ovarian edema and lacks distinct supporting evidence

rejected.label: Meigs syndrome
rejected.why: Lack of ascites and other characteristic findings

rejected.label: Uterine Fibroids
rejected.why: While present, they do not explain the adnexal mass

rejected.label: Lymphedema
rejected.why: While present, it is not the primary diagnosis explaining the adnexal mass
